newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder to sell five newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder to sell five newspapers.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc. said Friday it intends to sell five small-market newspapers in order to concentrate on its large-market newspapers and increase its financial flexibility.

The newspapers for sale are the Press-Telegram in Long Beach, Calif.; the Post-Tribune in Gary, Ind.; the Boca Raton News in Boca Raton, Fla.; The Union-Recorder in Milledgeville, Ga.; and The Newberry Observer in Newberry, S.C.
The Miami-based publisher, whose papers include The Philadelphia Inquirer and The Miami Herald, said it hopes to complete the sale in the fall, but it did not speculate on the proceeds.
The decision follows Knight-Ridder's recent acquisition of four newspapers from The Walt Disney Co. and a subsequent review of every property in its portfolio.
In order to buy newspapers in Kansas City, Mo.; Fort Worth, Texas, and two smaller cities, Knight-Ridder assumed debt of nearly $1 billion," Chairman and CEO Tony Ridder said .
"In addition, we are committed to the repurchase of more than 17 million shares of Knight-Ridder stock within the next 12 months."
The company had already announced the sale of Knight-Ridder Information to help reduce this debt load.
Lee Dirks of Dirks, Van Essen and Associates will be handling the sale for Knight-Ridder, the company said.

Knight-Ridder is also engaged in online publishing, business information services, electronic retrieval services and graphics and photo services. It publishes 35 daily newspapers in the United States, with a readership of 9.5 million daily and 13.6 million Sunday, and 35 Web sites.
Knight-Ridder stock fell 50 cents to $46.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
